We are all familiar with blockchains and bitcoins. Another thing we might not be familiar with is how exchanges work. Stock sales have options and larger traders have expedited sales. An interesting consequence of a distributed ledger is that everyone has a recorded copy of sales at the time they're made, which is 100% different than how the stock market works.

Human traders enter buy and sell orders in the order they get it but software exists that makes transactions in fractions of seconds. That undermines human trading and creates a hierarchy where larger traders get preferential treatment over small traders. Blockchain could end the dominance of large traders.

Also, totally unrelated but it only occurred to me recently that the UK developed computers first because they needed a way to abstract automated looms for their textile industry.
Only recently did I realize a huge benefit of how a distributed ledger works
